sections.heading: Getting started
paragraphs: Dina and his friend planned a fresh dinner at home. They talked about ingredients, cooking steps, and personal preferences. Dina said, “I am getting hungry.” His friend replied, “What would you like to eat?” Dina said, “I would like something healthy.” His friend replied, “Do you have any fresh fruit?” Dina said, “I usually eat breakfast early.” His friend replied, “I prefer water with my meal.” Dina said, “Could I have a glass of water?” His friend replied, “I do not want any added sugar.” Dina said, “This food smells delicious.” They paused for a moment to remember each expression.

sections.heading: A useful exchange
paragraphs: As they continued, they learned to explain what they needed. Dina said, “What ingredients are in this dish?” His friend replied, “It contains rice and vegetables.” Dina said, “I would like some chicken, please.” His friend replied, “Is the soup hot?” Dina said, “Please let it cool a little.” His friend replied, “I like spicy food.” Dina said, “This sauce is too spicy for me.” His friend replied, “Could you add less salt?” Dina said, “The salad tastes fresh.” They paused for a moment to remember each expression.

sections.heading: Making it clearer
paragraphs: They listened, asked questions, and tried the next useful expressions. Dina said, “I am allergic to this ingredient.” His friend replied, “Please check the ingredients for me.” Dina said, “I am trying a new recipe.” His friend replied, “First, wash the vegetables.” Dina said, “Then cut them into small pieces.” His friend replied, “Heat the pan over medium heat.” Dina said, “Cook the chicken thoroughly.” His friend replied, “I think the meal is ready.” Dina said, “Would you like another serving?” They paused for a moment to remember each expression.

sections.heading: Ending well
paragraphs: Before leaving, they finished the conversation warmly. Dina said, “No, thank you; I am full.” His friend replied, “Can we save the leftovers?” Dina said, “Put them in the refrigerator.” His friend replied, “I will wash the dishes later.” Dina said, “That was a satisfying meal.” His friend replied, “Thank you for cooking today.” Dina said, “Let us have dinner together tomorrow.” They felt more confident after practising together.
